new_statements.quote: 3. Stress. Contrastive stress occurs on the first or second syllable of stems. The following examples demonstrate these contrasts on two syllable words. /'ema/ I will see — /e'ma/ they; /'uta/ they did — /u'ta/ he is doing; /'ina/ white — /i'na/ fire; /'yana/ we are — /ya'na/ spear it!

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Yareba has an empty rule field and there are no existing statements, so this statement fills the gap rather than agreeing or contradicting: contrastive stress limited to the first two syllables of the stem. Quote verified against the page image (scanned/), not only the scanned text, which garbles the end of the first sentence.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is contrastive (phonemic) and falls on either the first or the second syllable of the stem; minimal pairs of disyllables differ only in stress position, so placement is not predictable from syllable count or shape (all syllables are open CV/CVV/V/VV).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the section is four lines plus four minimal pairs, restricted to stems (affixed forms not discussed).
new_statements.identity_note: Weimer & Weimer 1972 was collected in the village of Bibira, middle Musa Valley (Yareba proper; the 1973 NT is labelled 'Middle Musa dialect' in Glottolog). The two unread SIL manuscripts cover the whole Yareban family (Yareba, Aga Bereho/Bariji, Aneme Wake, Moikodi, Sirio/Nawaru per the Glottolog hh records), so if read later any stress statement in them must be checked for which language it refers to.

sources.quote: p.56: 'Contrastive stress occurs on the first or second syllable of stems. The following examples demonstrate these contrasts on two syllable words. /'ema/ I will see : /e'ma/ they; /'uta/ they did : /u'ta/ he is doing; /'ina/ white : /i'na/ fire; /'yana/ we are : /ya'na/ spear it!'. p.54: labialised consonants occur only preceding stressed vowels; p.55: /a/ is [a] in stressed, schwa-like in unstressed syllables; p.57: a stressed high vocoid is syllabic.

sources.note: The primary phoneme statement the 1975 sketch defers to (fn.4); its sec. 3 gives minimal pairs and restricts contrastive stress to the first or second syllable of stems, a window restriction absent from our the primary-stress rule.
